summary:
SOJOURNER: THE LITTLE ROVER WITH A BIG DREAM is an animated educational storybook designed for children aged 7–9 to explore NASA’s Mars Pathfinder mission and the Sojourner rover. Through an imaginative adventure featuring two young space detectives, Alex and Amy, and their friendly robot companion, Beep, children discover the story of this historic robotic explorer.

Combining colourful cartoon animations, character dialogues, narration and authentic NASA photographs, the project introduces the purpose of the Mars Pathfinder mission, Sojourner’s six-wheeled design, three cameras and scientific instrument, the Alpha Proton X-ray Spectrometer (APXS). Children learn that APXS is a scientific instrument used to identify the chemical elements found in Martian rocks and soil, helping scientists understand the composition of the Martian surface. They also discover how Sojourner communicated with Earth through Pathfinder and how its planned seven-day mission extended to 83 days.

To enrich the learning experience, our team created an original AI-generated theme song specifically for the animated storybook. By combining real NASA mission information, imaginative storytelling and music, the project aims to preserve the legacy of Mars exploration while inspiring curiosity, creativity and interest in robotics and STEM among young learners.
details:
SOJOURNER: THE LITTLE ROVER WITH A BIG DREAM

An AI-Powered Educational Storytelling Experience with an Original AI-Generated Song

1. What does your project do or how does it work?

Our project is an AI-assisted educational storytelling experience designed to introduce children aged 7–9 to NASA's Mars exploration mission through the story of Sojourner, the first successful rover to explore Mars. The story follows two young Space Detectives, Alex and Amy, who discover Sojourner and take the audience on an exciting journey to learn about its mission, discoveries and contributions to space exploration.

Through a 19-page illustrated digital storybook, children learn about Sojourner's six wheels, three cameras, Alpha Proton X-ray Spectrometer (APXS), communication system and exploration of Martian rocks and soil. The story also introduces important mission milestones, including Pathfinder's landing on 4 July 1997, Sojourner's deployment on 6 July 1997, and its remarkable 83-day operation despite being designed for a seven-day mission.

To make the learning experience more engaging, we incorporate an original AI-generated song related to Sojourner's journey. The song adds a musical dimension to the storytelling, helping children connect emotionally with the subject and remember important scientific facts. The story concludes with interactive thinking prompts that encourage children to observe, ask questions and think like young scientists.

2. What benefits does your project have?

  • Makes space science accessible: Simplifies historical and technical information about NASA's Mars mission into child-friendly language.
  • Promotes scientific curiosity: Encourages children to observe rocks, soil, shapes, colours and textures, and develop their own scientific questions.
  • Enhances memory and engagement: Combines storytelling, colourful illustrations and an AI-generated song to reinforce learning.
  • Develops critical thinking: Encourages children to investigate, compare, question and make observations rather than simply memorising facts.
  • Supports inclusive learning: Provides visual, auditory and narrative learning experiences to accommodate different learning preferences.
  • Inspires future exploration: Introduces children to space science, robotics, engineering and STEM-related careers.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our intended impact is to inspire the next generation of young explorers by making space science more accessible, enjoyable and meaningful.

We hope to transform children's perception of science from something that is difficult and abstract into an exciting adventure filled with discovery and imagination.

By introducing Sojourner's historical mission, we also aim to raise awareness of the scientific equipment and robotic technology that made early Mars exploration possible.

Ultimately, we want children to develop curiosity, creativity, critical thinking and an interest in STEM. Our key message is: Every great discovery begins with curiosity!

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?

The project was developed using AI-assisted digital content creation and multimedia production tools.

  • Canva: For designing and assembling the 19-page illustrated digital storybook.
  • AI image generation tools by ChatGPT: For creating colourful, cartoon-style illustrations of Sojourner, Mars, Alex, Amy and the supporting space environment.
  • AI music generation tools by AI Song Maker : For composing an original song that complements the storyline and reinforces the educational message.
  • NASA educational resources: For researching and verifying historical mission information, rover features and scientific discoveries.
  • Digital multimedia presentation by Canva and Dola AI: For combining visual storytelling, written content and music into one educational experience.

5. How is your project creative?

The creativity of our project lies in transforming NASA's historical space exploration information into a child-friendly adventure. Instead of presenting scientific facts through conventional slides or lectures, we introduce two fictional Space Detectives, Alex and Amy, who guide children through the discovery of Sojourner.

Our creative elements include:

  • Character-based storytelling: Alex and Amy act as young investigators, making the scientific journey relatable to children.
  • AI-generated illustrations: Cartoon-style visuals bring the Mars environment, rover and scientific discoveries to life.
  • Original AI-generated song: Music adds emotion, rhythm and another way for children to remember the story.
  • Science detective approach: Children are encouraged to investigate Martian rocks and soil by observing their shapes, colours and textures.
  • Interactive thinking questions: The story invites children to predict, question and explore rather than passively receive information.
  • Integration of history and imagination: Real NASA mission facts are presented through an imaginative narrative without losing their educational value.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered several important factors during the development of the project:

  1. Target audience: We designed the content for children aged 7–9, using simple vocabulary, short explanations and attractive illustrations.
  2. Scientific accuracy: We referred to NASA's mission information to ensure that the historical facts about Sojourner and Mars Pathfinder were represented accurately.
  3. Educational value: Every storytelling section was designed to communicate specific scientific knowledge and encourage curiosity.
  4. Engagement and enjoyment: We combined storytelling, characters, illustrations and AI-generated music to maintain children's interest.
  5. Accessibility: We considered different learning preferences by integrating visual, auditory and reading experiences.
  6. Creativity and originality: We developed our own narrative, characters and song to create a distinctive educational experience.
  7. Technology integration: We explored how AI tools could support educational content creation while ensuring that technology enhanced rather than replaced scientific understanding.

Through this project, we hope to demonstrate that artificial intelligence can be used creatively and responsibly to transform scientific knowledge into an engaging learning adventure.

Our message: Small rover, big dream, endless discoveries!
